next_question.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Activate emergency help and provide effective bag-mask ventilations while naloxone is obtained and administered.","B":"Leave the client to retrieve naloxone before initiating ventilation because antidote delivery takes priority.","C":"Stop the opioid infusion and apply nasal oxygen, then wait several minutes for spontaneous respirations to improve.","D":"Place the client in recovery position and reassess after naloxone arrives, avoiding assisted ventilation meanwhile."}}
next_question.rationale: For suspected opioid overdose with severe respiratory depression or respiratory arrest and a definite pulse, ventilation and emergency-system activation must not be delayed while naloxone is obtained or administered. Naloxone is important, but airway and breathing support are immediate priorities. Stopping the opioid or applying oxygen without adequate ventilation does not correct profound hypoventilation.
next_question.source_detail: Section 21.11: provide breaths/bag-mask ventilation with definite pulse; do not delay standard resuscitation for naloxone
